title: The basement stairs
intake: Adult male, 45, found at the bottom of the basement stairs at 23:10.
context: His wife called for help, saying he fell down the stairs about an hour earlier.
note: This case involves a violent death. Findings are described clinically.

procedures.name: Scene investigation
procedures.blurb: The stairs, the basement, what his wife says.

procedures.name: External exam
procedures.blurb: Examine the body region by region.

procedures.name: Toxicology (rush)
procedures.blurb: Drugs and alcohol in the blood.

procedures.name: Skeletal survey (X-ray)
procedures.blurb: Old and new fractures across the whole skeleton.

findings.label: Wife's account
findings.text: Wife: he fell down the stairs about an hour before she called, at 23:05.
findings.meaning: Her account puts death within the last hour or so. Check it against the body.

findings.label: Stairs
findings.text: Eleven wooden steps. No blood or marks on the steps or walls; blood only on the floor under his head.
findings.meaning: A tumbling fall usually leaves blood or marks on the way down. Injuries only at the bottom don't fit the story well.

findings.label: Rigor
findings.text: Stiff jaw and arms; legs still loose.
findings.meaning: Rigor is still spreading: roughly 3.5–8.5 hours.

findings.label: Livor
findings.text: Purple-red on the back; blanches under thumb pressure.
findings.meaning: Visible but not fixed: roughly 2–10 hours.

findings.label: Top of head
findings.text: Three lacerations on the top of the head, all above the hat brim line.
findings.meaning: Falls usually injure the head at or below the hat brim line. Several injuries above it are typical of blows.

findings.label: Forearms
findings.text: Bruises on the backs of both forearms.
findings.meaning: Defense injuries: bruises from raising the arms to ward off blows.

findings.label: Skull and brain
findings.text: A depressed fracture of the top of the skull, with bleeding over the brain beneath it and no bruising on the opposite side of the brain.
findings.meaning: Injury under the impact with none opposite it (coup without contrecoup) means a moving object struck a still head: a blow, not a fall.

findings.label: Stomach
findings.meaning: No recent meal to time from. Empty stomachs say little on their own.

findings.label: Toxicology
findings.meaning: Far too little alcohol to explain a fall or a death.

findings.label: Skeleton
findings.text: No old fractures; no new fractures apart from the skull.
findings.meaning: A fall down eleven stairs often fractures an arm, wrist or ribs. Only the skull is broken.

causes.label: Blunt force injuries of the head from blows
Head injury from a fall down stairs

person: Tomás Ortiz, 45, a high-school chemistry teacher.
story: He died at about 17:10, some six hours before the call, from blows to the top of his head. The body's timeline and injuries didn't match the account of a fall an hour earlier. Homicide on a death certificate means death at the hands of another person; it is a medical finding, not a legal verdict, and what happened next is for the police and the courts.
